card: Bitcoin Core now ignores BIP35 mempool messages from peers with transaction relay disabled unless they hold the mempool network permission. Inbound peers advertising fRelay=false bypass the inbound transaction-relay capacity limits introduced in #28463, yet can currently extract full mempool inventory on nodes with bloom filters enabled. Requiring transaction relay to be active closes this accounting bypass while preserving SPV clients that load a BIP37 bloom filter before querying the mempool.
changed_since_previous: Added release notes and updated BIP documentation; the core logic and test coverage remain unchanged.
evidence: PR description: 'When a node offers NODE_BLOOM, an inbound peer can advertise fRelay=false and request BIP35 mempool inventory while remaining outside the inbound transaction-relay capacity introduced in #28463.'

Commit 33a678ca5b: 'An inbound peer with fRelay=false stays outside transaction-relay capacity accounting, yet BIP35 requests give it full mempool inventory. Ignore these requests until transaction relay is enabled, except when the operator grants the mempool permission.'
problem: When a node has bloom filtering enabled, an inbound peer can connect with fRelay=false to stay outside the inbound transaction-relay capacity limits introduced in #28463 while still downloading full mempool inventory through BIP35 requests.

risk.why: A mistake in peer state validation could break mempool synchronization for legitimate SPV clients or permissioned inbound peers.

summary: Ignores BIP35 mempool protocol messages from peers that have transaction relay disabled (such as via fRelay=false), unless the peer has been granted the mempool network permission. Peers can still receive mempool inventory once transaction relay is enabled, such as after loading a BIP37 filter, which subjects the connection to inbound transaction-relay capacity accounting.
